title: Morning Edition
dek: Mali’s army suffered one of its worst recent battlefield losses; Saudi Arabia has restarted its strategic Red Sea oil bypass; Lithuania is designing a power substation for drone warfare; and the Ideas desk asks whether morality can be universal without denying cultural difference.

lead_story.headline: More than 100 Malian soldiers were reportedly killed when JNIM overran a central Mali army camp
lead_story.summary: Reuters, citing security and military sources, reports that more than 100 Malian soldiers were killed in the September 10 assault on the Dioura camp. Al-Qaeda-linked JNIM has published higher claims and video of captured soldiers; Mali’s army acknowledges losses but has not issued a comparable public toll.
lead_story.why_it_matters: The scale of the loss suggests a serious deterioration in Mali’s campaign against JNIM despite years of military rule and Russian security support. The exact toll and number captured remain uncertain, so the edition treats the source-based estimate—not JNIM’s propaganda figures—as the strongest available account.
lead_story.original_language: English; French-language and local claims cross-checked

items.headline: Saudi Arabia has restarted its East–West oil pipeline, but only at a low rate so far
items.summary: Saudi Arabia resumed pumping through the East–West pipeline after a shutdown following drone attacks, Reuters reports. The line moves crude from eastern fields to the Red Sea and is especially important while Strait of Hormuz traffic remains disrupted.
items.why_it_matters: The route is Saudi Arabia’s main physical bypass around Hormuz. Even a partial restart restores redundancy to a global oil system that has recently been operating with less room for failure; full throughput has not yet been restored.

items.headline: Lithuania is designing a major power substation to survive explosive drones and sabotage
items.summary: The planned Gižai substation near Kaliningrad will use hardened transformer enclosures, duplicated equipment, anti-tunnelling sensors and other physical defenses. It will anchor the future Harmony Link connection with Poland.
items.why_it_matters: Europe’s energy-security problem is shifting from diversifying fuel supplies to physically hardening the grid itself. Gižai is a concrete example of civilian infrastructure being redesigned around lessons from attacks on Ukraine’s energy system.

items.headline: The EU is moving toward public energy-and-water efficiency labels for large data centres
items.summary: The European Commission proposed a common rating system for data centres above 500 kW, covering energy and water efficiency and contributions such as waste-heat reuse. Separate minimum performance standards are being prepared for 2027.
items.why_it_matters: Europe wants far more computing capacity for AI while grids and water systems face constraints. The label does not cap consumption, but it creates a measurement framework that can later support binding efficiency standards.

items.headline: Webb found chemical evidence that Neptune’s present moons may be debris from an ancient catastrophe
items.summary: James Webb Space Telescope observations found magnesium-rich clay minerals on several small inner moons and rings. Researchers argue the material likely came from a larger water-altered body destroyed after Neptune captured Triton.
items.why_it_matters: It offers a physical clue to why Neptune’s moon system looks so unlike the orderly satellite systems of the other giant planets: Triton’s capture may have demolished much of the original system and rebuilt it from debris.

items.headline: Can morality be universal without pretending cultures are morally identical?
items.summary: Susan Neiman reviews Steven Lukes’s attempt to hold two truths together: human moral practices vary enormously, yet describing that variation cannot by itself tell us that every practice is equally justified. The dispute turns on the gap between explaining a norm and giving it moral authority.
items.why_it_matters: Relativism and universalism often talk past one another because one side points to empirical diversity while the other asks a normative question. The essay clarifies why discovering what societies value is not the same as deciding what anyone ought to value.
items.source: The New York Review of Books

items.headline: Bogotá’s Palenquero community is spending a week bringing its language, food, music and memory into public space
items.summary: The city’s seventh Palenquero Diaspora Week began September 21 with discussions, performances, food, film and theater organized with the community descended from San Basilio de Palenque. Events foreground Palenquero, the Afro-Colombian creole language, alongside the community’s history in Bogotá.
items.why_it_matters: The stakes are intentionally local: a diaspora community maintaining a language and social memory in the city where it now lives. After recent stops in East and southern Africa, Southeast Asia, Latin America, East Asia, Syria and Guam, this returns to Latin America through an urban Afro-Colombian community rather than national news.
items.source: Bogotá District Government / Palenquero community organizers

worth_your_time.headline: What is literary criticism actually for?
worth_your_time.summary: Colin Burrow uses the shrinking institutional home of English literature as a reason to ask what criticism contributes when it is not merely ranking books or decoding them for specialists. The essay turns the crisis of university English into a broader argument about judgment, attention and the usefulness of learning how to describe why a work succeeds or fails.
worth_your_time.why_it_matters: It is a durable question about expertise: criticism matters less as a warehouse of approved interpretations than as disciplined practice in noticing, comparing and making judgments that can be argued with.

notes_for_next_edition: Mali: return for an official casualty accounting, verified hostage outcome, major territorial change or strategic response—not repeated militant claims.
Saudi pipeline: return for verified restoration of substantial/full capacity or another material disruption.
EU data centres: return when minimum standards are proposed or the label produces meaningful compliance data.
Human Scale: after Bogotá prioritize Caribbean, South Asia, rural Europe outside France, or Africa outside the recent sequence.
